'''George D. Gollin''' (born May 6, 1953) is an American [[physics]] professor at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. Besides his work on particle physics and the International Linear Collider, he has since 2003 made numerous efforts in fighting institutions which are considered to be [[diploma mills]], which has caused him to receive significant public attention. Gollin placed second in the 2014 Democratic primary for [[Illinois's 13th congressional district]].<ref name=roll>{{cite news|last=Cahn|first=Emily|title=Ann Callis, Rodney Davis to Face Off in Targeted Illinois District|url=http://atr.rollcall.com/ann-callis-rodney-davis-illinois-primary/|accessdate=19 March 2014|newspaper=Roll Call|date=2014-03-18|archive-date=2014-03-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140319132512/http://atr.rollcall.com/ann-callis-rodney-davis-illinois-primary/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Areas of research and teaching==
Gollin has worked on [[particle physics]] experiments studying [[muon]] scattering (1975–1981, intended to test the ideas of "[[Quantum Chromodynamics]]"), neutral [[K meson]] decay parameters (1980–1993, measuring things relating to "[[K meson#CP violation in neutral meson oscillations|CP violation]]"), and [[electron-positron annihilation]] (1993–2005, measuring production and decay properties of [[heavy quarks]]). His current research focuses on technical issues associated with the design and construction of the "[[International Linear Collider]]", a very large electron-positron colliding beams facility intended to shed light on the origins of the masses of the fundamental particles.

His teaching has spanned the entire physics curriculum, from elementary [[algebra]]-based courses for students in the life sciences to classical [[electrodynamics]] at the graduate level.

==Other public service==
The University of Illinois is a [[public university]] and "[[Land-grant university|land grant school]]"; as such, Gollin's responsibilities include faculty [[community service|public service]] in addition to his teaching and research obligations.<ref>''q.v.'' ''[http://www.oc.uiuc.edu/engagement/p&tfacultyguide2000.pdf A Faculty Guide for Relating Public Service to the Promotion and Tenure Review Process]'', University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign</ref> Since 2003, Gollin has been documenting the practices of alleged diploma mills, which are believed to sell meaningless academic degrees without providing education or assessment to/of their customers.<ref name=chicagotribune>[http://www.chicagotribune.com/business/content/education/chi-diploma-mill-04-aug04,0,2164133.story Bogus diploma ring busted with help from U. of I. professor], By Russell Working, [[Chicago Tribune]], August 4, 2008 {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080807024912/http://www.chicagotribune.com/business/content/education/chi-diploma-mill-04-aug04,0,2164133.story |date=August 7, 2008 }}</ref> In this capacity, he has worked with a number of state and federal agencies, including the State of Washington Office of the Attorney General, the U.S. Dept. of Education, the U.S. Secret Service, and the Swedish National Agency for Higher Education.<ref name=chicagotribune/><ref>"[https://www.cbsnews.com/news/cracking-down-on-diploma-mills/ Cracking Down on Diploma Mills]," CBS News Special Report: Consumer Alert, 25 July 2003.</ref> It was reported in ''[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]'' that "Alan Contreras, administrator for the [[Oregon Office of Degree Authorization]], called the professor's work 'superb'."<ref name=chron>[http://chronicle.com/article/U-of-Illinois-Administrators/111307/ "U. of Illinois Administrators Ask Professor to Remove Web Site About Diploma Mills"], by Andrea L. Foster, ''[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]'', October 13, 2003{{Subscription required}}</ref> He has, for example, assisted with the federal investigation of the operation of an alleged diploma mill, [[Saint Regis University]].<ref>[[Saint Regis University]] should not be confused with the legitimate, [[Accreditation|accredited]] [[Regis University]] of Denver, Colorado.</ref> This investigation resulted in closing down the large operation and the conviction on federal criminal charges of eight individuals who were involved.<ref name="HigherEdSup">Phillips, Stephen. [http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=199963&sectioncode=26 "A stress-free PhD? A snip at $250"], ''[[The Higher Education Supplement]]'' 25 November 2005</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Diploma Mill Ringleader Gets Maximum Sentence |url=https://www.kxly.com/diploma-mill-ringleader-gets-maximum-sentence/ |accessdate=22 April 2020 |work=[[KXLY-TV]] |date=2 July 2008 |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120909005001/http://www.kxly.com/news/21378873/detail.html |archivedate=2012-09-09 |url-status=unfit}}</ref>{{cbignore|bot=InternetArchiveBot}}

In 2006 he was elected to the board of directors of the [[Council for Higher Education Accreditation]] for a three-year term. He was reelected to a second term in 2009.<ref>[http://chea.org/news/NR_2009.05.05.htm CHEA Announces New and Reelected Board Members] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090813093901/http://www.chea.org/news/NR_2009.05.05.htm |date=2009-08-13 }}, [[CHEA]]</ref> Also in 2009 Gollin was named a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] by the [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]]. George Gollin said of the fellowship, "I will use the term of the Fellowship to write a book about the nine-year trajectory and spectacular immolation of [[Saint Regis University|St. Regis]], and the resulting increase in international attention to the problem of diploma mills."<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/16488-george-d-gollin Fellowships to Assist Research and Artistic Creation] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090611090559/http://www.gf.org/fellows/16488-george-d-gollin |date=2009-06-11 }}, George D. Gollin, [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]]</ref>

==2014 U.S. House campaign==
{{See also|United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois, 2014#District 13}}
Gollin announced in July 2013 his intention to run for the Illinois 13th Congressional District.<ref>[http://www.news-gazette.com/news/local/2013-07-23/ui-physicist-joins-race-13th-district.html UI physicist joins race for 13th District], [[The News-Gazette (Champaign-Urbana)]], 23 July 2013</ref> He faced [[Ann Callis]] and David Green in the Democratic Party primary on March 18, 2014. Gollin was endorsed by the ''[[The News-Gazette (Champaign-Urbana)|News-Gazette]]'', ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', and the ''[[State Journal-Register]]''.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kacich|first=Tom|title=Many Dems rally behind Callis in congressional primary, but papers endorsing Gollin|url=http://www.news-gazette.com/news/local/2014-03-16/many-dems-rally-behind-callis-congressional-primary-papers-endorsing-gollin.ht|accessdate=18 March 2014|newspaper=News-Gazette|date=2014-03-16}}</ref> According to ''[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]'', Gollin "isn't seen by Washington Democrats as a strong candidate."<ref>{{cite news|last=Joseph|first=Cameron|title=Eyes on Illinois on Tuesday night|url=https://thehill.com/blogs/ballot-box/201110-eyes-on-illinois-on-tuesday-night/|access-date=18 March 2014|newspaper=The Hill|date=2014-03-18}}</ref>
